description: Check O-singleton-read-safety using the constructed crash history and a stronger sync-all control. Compare actual read response against prior completed write after caller application strictly passes the returned fence.

harness.description: Actual singleton protocol prefix, modeled required durable flushes, reconstruction and register application; no private state substitution.
semantic_changes: Separate caller-owned staged and durable storage copies simulate permitted loss of non-synchronized metadata.
In-memory register resets to its actual saved snapshot and replays ordered committed entries.
Control flushes all Ready batches; main history flushes every MustSync batch.

legality.derivation: Bootstrap configuration is committed/applied and an actual snapshot is created at that point. Self-election and both writes use public RawNode APIs. Each Ready appends entries and stages nonempty HardState before Advance. On every required sync, all previous staged HardState plus every stored log entry is copied to the durable model, so later writes cannot retroactively lose a prior flush. With MustSync=false only commit metadata can be lost; log entries and term/vote changes force sync. Two proposals before Ready share an actual durable append. The caller emits write completion only after the register applies B. Restart creates a new MemoryStorage from the saved real snapshot, checkpointed entries and checkpointed HardState, resets volatile application to snapshot state, and drains replay before campaigning. The read arrives after becoming leader but before processing the new leader entry; calls are serialized. The application respects Ready order, applies one bounded batch at a time and waits for applied > ReadState.Index, then records the read before further replay. No private protocol state is read or changed. RawNode has no background resource to shut down.
legality.applicability: Explicit simulated crash/storage durability model; no loss of synchronized state or arbitrary manufactured history. Register state is intentionally volatile and reconstructed from durable snapshot and committed log.
alternatives: Syncing every Ready is the stronger control and must not be imposed as an unstated requirement on the minimum-sync history.

grounding.derivation: The prior write completion records the actually applied register value after both writes have been committed and applied. Read invocation follows crash/restart and refers to that completion index. No later writes occur. The returned ReadState is obtained from real Ready and correlated by unique request context; the caller serves only when its actual applied index is strictly greater than the fence. Hence the completed result must equal the latest prior completed write value. Result identity uses history, not value or commit context. The sync-all control changes only caller durability policy and is checked by the same oracle.
grounding.applicability: Two independent one-voter histories, one honoring minimum MustSync and one additionally syncing every Ready. A crash retains actual checkpointed durable snapshot/log/HardState. No current-term fence or completion is assumed.
alternatives: ReadIndex may be dropped; absence remains incomplete and is not an incorrect-value witness.
Later replay restoring B does not retroactively change the earlier completed response.

observable_properties.description: With no intervening writes, the completed register read after a completed pre-crash write must return that write value once caller read-fence duties are met.

uncertainties: Crash model is a simulation of the documented sync boundary, not a physical disk power-loss test.
The safety conclusion is limited to returned and served reads, not request completion guarantees.
